text:
maria: Heads up — our H100 canary is spiking errors after the driver/ CUDA 538 roll yesterday. TensorRT/FlashAttention loads are failing intermittently.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy/h100-driver-538 started at 1865129000, status=completed, pods=3

jon: seeing a 3.8x latency spike and ~45% 5xx on the canary route (region: us-west2). Autometrics alert fired.

lee: any obvious logs from the trt container? could be PTX/driver mismatch.

jon: paste from one failing pod log:
```
[trt_plugin] ERROR: failed to initialize plugin libflash_attention.so: undefined symbol: _ZN12flash_attn...
TRT ERROR: plugin load failed, falling back to CPU path
E inference: cudaDriverGetVersion returned CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN
E inference: PTX compilation rejected: ptx version 9.3 rejects for device sm_90
```

sam: that looks like PTX/driver ABI mismatch — 538 is more strict about ptx/ptxv. FlashAttention native kernels and some xFormers builds ship PTX that now gets rejected.

lee: confirmed on node: nvidia-driver=538.12, cuda-runtime=12.2, trt=8.6.1, flash-attn built with nvcc targeting ptx 9.2.

maria: how many hosts are affected? only canary or broader?

jon: only canary pool so far (3 H100 nodes) — but if we push to eu-west it’ll hit more. Dedicated capacity customers on h100-dedicated pools are still on 537 image.

sam: short-term mitigation: 1) pin inference pods to run TRT CPU fallback (degrades perf) 2) redeploy tensors with plugins built against 538 PTX target 3) rollback driver to 537 on canary nodes.

lee: CPU fallback will increase cost and latency dramatically for canary traffic — not great for SLAs. Rollback seems fastest.

jon: also seeing NCCL warnings during heavy fanout, probably a symptom of driver mismatch too. Example:
```
NCCL WARN Net/detect: Incompatible CUDA IPC support, fallback to proxy
```

maria: action proposal: rollback driver->537 on the 3 canary nodes now, hold the fleet upgrade, and open an infra-incident. Also add matrix tests for PTX/Trt/FlashAttn combos before future rollouts.

sam: +1. I'll open an issue and start a quick rebuild of flash-attn/xformers wheels targeting ptx 9.3 so we have a non-rollback path.

deploy-bot: canary-rollback/h100-driver -> started at 1865130200, rolling restart 3 nodes

lee: pinged cloud provider; they show the 538 driver image as available but we'll need to coordinate canary scheduling to avoid mass reprovisioning.

jon: cost note — if we do CPU fallback for even a day, Dedicated commit meters will spike for some routes due to longer token times. estimate +18% token cost if we route canary traffic to fallback.

maria: OK rollback in progress. lee, coordinate with infra to ensure rollback doesn't trigger other automation. sam, keep working on the rebuilt plugin artifacts. i'll file an incident with severity P2 and schedule a postmortem once we stabilize.

sam: also recommend adding a tiny compile-time test to our model infra CI: build minimal FlashAttn plugin and run it in a CUDA 538 emulated env to catch PTX rejections earlier.

lee: will add matrix job. Also we should capture a list of images + kernel abi permutations that passed previously so upgrades can be gated.

maria: thanks — will update on status in 20. current plan: rollback canary -> verify latency/error -> hold fleet upgrade and bake compatibility tests.

jon: verified: one pod restarted and is now healthy after rollback on node-3, latency trending down.

maria: nice. keep me posted. :thumbsup:
